advisory.summary: Ghost's integrations endpoints granted every authenticated staff user, a Contributor included, the integration list with each integration's admin API key secret.
note: GHSA-j5c2-hm46-wp5c. core/server/models/integration.js overrode
permissible() to add the hosted customIntegrations limit check and then
`return true` -- discarding the permission answer it was overriding. So
GET /ghost/api/v4/admin/integrations/ served any authenticated staff
user, and ?include=api_keys handed them every integration's ADMIN API key
secret, which is an escalation to full Admin on the API. 4.10.0 takes
hasUserPermission/hasApiKeyPermission and throws NoPermissionError.
The permission hook read as enforcing and returned true regardless.
Confirmed from the source INSIDE both images: 4.9.4's permissible ends
`return true;` and the file holds no `hasUserPermission`; 4.10.0's throws
on it. A `customIntegrations` grep found 2 lines in each file, so the
empty result was a grep that could have found something. package.json
reads 4.9.4 and 4.10.0, so neither tag is a hotfix build of something
else.
Ghost's Admin API authenticates a staff user with a signed session
cookie, so each identity is a static Cookie header, minted through the
app's own /session/ endpoint.
Measured by hand on both tags before this was written: the contributor
reads /integrations/?include=api_keys 200 with the marker and every admin
key secret on 4.9.4, and 403 without the marker on 4.10.0. Its session is
valid on 4.10.0 -- /users/me/, /posts/ and /settings/ all 200 -- so the
403 is the fix, not a refused credential, and the provisioner asserts the
account's only role is Contributor so the attacker cannot be entitled. No
cookie and a fabricated cookie are both 403 on both builds, which is why
the credential's evidence is those 200s and not a status on this route.
The second check is the single-integration route, measured on both tags
rather than inferred from the list: the contributor reads the owner's
integration by id 200 with the marker on 4.9.4 and 403 without it on
4.10.0, while the owner is 200 with the marker on both.
There is no allowed route to the marker either: 27 admin routes were
swept with the contributor's session on 4.10.0, 11 of them answered 200
-- /settings/, /config/, /site/, /users/, /users/me/, /posts/, /pages/,
/tags/, /themes/, /roles/, /snippets/ -- and none carried the marker,
while /db/, the content export that would hold it, is 403. The owner's
session over those same 27 routes answered 200 on 20 and carried the
marker on exactly two, /integrations/ and /integrations/?include=api_keys,
so the contributor's zero is an absence and not a detector that cannot
fire. A count of four routes did not reproduce, and the routes are named
here because a bare count is a claim no test can diff.
The third check is the contributor reading its own profile, the request
the provisioner already makes on both builds to assert the Contributor
role. It is there for the patched build: the leaking routes are 403 to a
fabricated cookie too, so without a 200 somewhere in the run Veridor
records the contributor's 403s as unproven and the harness fails the pair
rather than certify a fix against a session that might be dead.

checks.name: A Contributor must not read the integration list or its admin API key secrets
A Contributor must not read the owner's integration by id
The Contributor's session is one Ghost recognises, as the owner's is
